evidence: Receiving DO2 at 52.0 h = 4.32 mg/L, down from 10.24 mg/L at 50.0 h (~3 mg/L/h decline)
Receiving P(48 h) = 2.88 g/L, comparable to source P(48 h) ≈ 3.0 g/L — product on track
Source batches maintain DO2 ≈ 10.8–11.5 mg/L at 50–52 h; receiving deviates sharply below
Minimum DO2 constraint = 2.0 mg/L; projected breach in ~4–5 h without intervention
Allowed action bounds: combined = feed scale 0.8, air scale 1.15
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 dropped from ~10.5 to ~4.3 mg/L between 50 and 52 h while product (P=2.88 g/L at 48 h) tracks the source batches, indicating oxygen demand is outstripping transfer at peak growth. Without action DO2 will breach the 2.0 mg/L minimum within ~4–5 h, forfeiting product. A 15% air increase alone may not arrest the steep decline; a 20% feed reduction plus 15% aeration increase (combined) cuts OUR and raises OTR, giving the largest safe margin while retaining 80% of feed and most product mass.
submission.uncertainty: The future oxygen-uptake trajectory is hidden; the 3 mg/L/h decline may stabilize on its own (as source dips did), in which case a feed cut sacrifices some product unnecessarily. Conversely, 15% extra air may be insufficient if OUR keeps growing. Delayed assays (4 h turnaround) and hidden states mean the 48 h P value may be stale by the decision time.

evidence: Receiving DO2 drops from 10.2 mg/L (t=50.0) to 4.86 (t=50.2) to 4.32 (t=52.0), versus ~10.5-11.5 mg/L in source-1/2/3 at the same batch age
Source-reference trajectory: identical DO2 profile shape pre-50h including induction dip to 7.3-8.6 mg/L at t=24-28
P assay at t=48 (avail 52): 2.88 g/L, comparable to sources (2.98-3.06 g/L)
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: below_limit_h=0, min DO 2.58 mg/L, 256.2 kg, 4/5 feasible sensitivity members
Forward model keep/reduce_feed/increase_air/combined all violate the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit (min DO 1.36-1.65)
Inferred oxygen transfer multiplier 0.5246 (model update at t=52)
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 diverges sharply from all three source batches at t~50h, collapsing from ~10.2 to ~4.3-4.9 mg/L and still falling, indicating a large step increase in oxygen demand the vessel cannot supply (inferred transfer multiplier ~0.52). Nominal source-calibrated forward model shows KEEP and milder actions breach the 2.0 mg/L oxygen limit (min DO 1.36-1.65 mg/L, 2.8-5.4 h below limit), whereas strong_feed_reduction keeps min DO at 2.58 mg/L with zero below-limit time, retains full product mass (~256 kg, the highest of all actions), and is feasible in 4/5 sensitivity members. Feed reduction targets the root cause (excess demand) rather than relying on limited aeration headroom; the 1.15x air bump adds margin. Stop would forfeit all counted production.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is nominal and source-calibrated, not the hidden evaluator realization; the 5-member sensitivity still includes realizations with min DO down to ~1.31 mg/L, so residual constraint risk exists. The DO crash onset (~50h) is recent, so the demand regime estimate is data-limited; if the DO decline is transient rather than sustained, strong feed reduction could cost some product versus keep. Assay delay (4h) and the fact that the process runs KEEP until any decision mean the DO may fall further before actuation. Product quality/impurity effects of feed cut are not observable from the available data.
